newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Harradine says could support Telstra sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Harradine says could support Telstra sale.

text.p: Key Australian Independent senator Brian Harradine said on Thursday he would support the partial sale of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp if all his concerns were met.
Those concerns included the method by which one-third of Telstra was sold, he said.
"Under those circumstances, if all of those matters were satisfactorily concluded, I would believe that I would be doing my duty in voting for the (bill)," he told parliament.

Harradine also repeated that he remained concerned about employment issues, the need for the island state of Tasmania to be technologically up-to-date, and recognition of Tasmania's pre-eminent natural heritage position. However, he said discussions with the government on these issues had gone well.

Harradine and fellow Independent Mal Colston are crucial to the passing of the Telstra sale legislation as they are the only possible sources of the two extra votes that the government needs to pass any legislation in the upper house Senate.
All other non-government parties are opposed to the sale.
The government plans to raise A$8 billion through the sale of one-third of Telstra with A$1 billion of the proceeds earmarked for an environment package.
